sentences.text: Flying into Jamaica's north coast, and not sure how you'll get from the airport to your hotel?
Three easy ways: a pre-booked private transfer, a taxi, or a rental car.
Let's get you to Ocho Rios.
Quick note: Aurum Transfers is a travel-affiliate brand, so if you book through our links we may earn a commission, at no extra cost to you. We don't run the rides ourselves; our partners do.
One honest note: some clips here were filmed before Hurricane Melissa in October 2025, so a few places may look different today.
Welcome to Ian Fleming International, Jamaica's newest international port of entry.
It sits in Boscobel, in the parish of Saint Mary, about fifteen kilometres east of Ocho Rios.
It has a single runway and serves private jets, charters and select international flights.
And yes, it's named after Ian Fleming, the creator of James Bond. His Jamaican home, GoldenEye, is about five kilometres away in Oracabessa.
This guide is for Ian Fleming. Jamaica's other two international airports, Sangster in Montego Bay and Norman Manley in Kingston, get their own arrival guides.
Is this your first time flying into the north coast? Tell us in the comments where you're staying.
Now, the timing. Customs and immigration here run daily from seven in the morning to seven in the evening, and outside those hours prior notice is required.
Before you fly, fill in the immigration and customs C5 form online, and make your customs declaration before you arrive.
Your passport must stay valid for your whole stay, and your airline's own rules may be stricter, so check with them too.
British visitors don't need a visa and are usually granted entry for up to ninety days. Other nationalities should check the rules for their own passport.
At customs, declare anything prohibited or subject to duty, and leave meat and dairy products at home.
If this checklist just saved you a headache, tap like; it tells us to make more arrival guides like this one.
Through customs? Here's how to get to your hotel.
The airport lists taxi or coach hire for getting around. Taxis are available on site when needed, for an extra fee.
Option one is the calmest: a pre-booked private transfer. Your driver is arranged before you land, so there's no hunting for a ride after your flight.
On aurum-transfers.com you can compare airport transfers from partner companies; the partner you choose runs the ride, so book once your flight times are fixed.
Option two, a taxi. Canada advises avoiding unmarked cars, and the UK advises using taxis approved by the Jamaica Tourist Board, which show a blue JTB sticker.
Option three, a rental car. Jamaica drives on the left, so take it slowly on the coast road.
Which one are you picking: transfer, taxi or rental? Tell us below, and the transfer comparison link is in the description.
Now, the best part: Ocho Rios and the coast around it.
Dunn's River is one of the few waterfalls in the world that empties straight into the sea.
Water shoes make the climb safer, and they're sold at the entrance if you forget yours.
Back in town, the bay is right there for a swim.
Further west along the coast is Runaway Bay, another resort area.
Waterfall first, then the beach: that's a good first day on the north coast.
A few last tips. Don't show off valuables, and never leave anything in a parked car.
The currency is the Jamaican dollar. Cards work at hotels and tourist businesses, but cash machines are limited outside Kingston and Montego Bay.
After Melissa damaged water systems in the west and south, the health ministry advised treating water before drinking it, so check the latest advice when you arrive.
So, the short version. Check the airport's hours, fill in your C5 form before you fly, and pick your ride before you land. Then enjoy the north coast.
Subscribe for the next arrival guide, and enjoy every minute on the north coast. See you on the next trip!
